claims.statement: oxyromon's Cargo features are default = ["use-rustls"], plus use-native-tls, mcp and server; `server` lists `mcp` among its dependencies so a --features server build also builds the MCP server (and rmcp/transport-streamable-http-server), while `mcp` alone builds only the stdio server.

use-rustls and use-native-tls are pure passthroughs to reqwest, which is declared default-features = false so no other dependency implies a TLS backend; nothing in Cargo.toml or build.rs asserts their mutual exclusion, so the operator must pick exactly one (e.g. --no-default-features --features use-native-tls, or --no-default-features --features use-rustls on Windows where asm-hashes break under MSVC).

src/main.rs gates whole modules with cfg(feature) — `mcp` for src/mcp.rs, `server` for mutation, query, server and validator — and gates the corresponding subcommand registrations and the post-scope server dispatch, so the argv surface shrinks with the feature set: `oxyromon mcp` and `oxyromon server` do not exist in a default build.

The features change runtime database behaviour, not just which code compiles: establish_connection uses cfg_if on any(feature = "server", feature = "mcp") to open a 5-connection pool with PRAGMA locking_mode = NORMAL, while every other build gets max_connections = 1 with EXCLUSIVE locking.

Server-only capability is threaded through otherwise-shared code: OxyromonMcp's sse_tx field, with_sse, mcp_http_service() and the sse_send fan-out in mcp/actions.rs are cfg(feature = "server") (the stdio build has no SseMessage at all); model.rs attaches GraphQL derives via cfg_attr and defines Dependency/GameInformation only under `server`; find_games_by_system_id_paged, process_dat_upload and ImportDatResult exist only under `server`.

The `server` feature pulls tower-http unconditionally, but the permissive CorsLayer is compiled only under cfg(debug_assertions); release server builds link the crate and serve without CORS, relying on the SPA and the desktop webview being same-origin.

build.rs rebuilds the web UI only when cfg!(feature = "server") and SKIP_TRUNK is not exactly the string "true"; it then runs `trunk build --release` with `frontend` as the working directory and fails the entire cargo build if that command exits non-zero.

Before shelling out to trunk, build.rs asserts that `frontend/` exists because `frontend/` is a nested package that cargo leaves out of the published tarball; Command reports a missing working directory exactly as it reports a missing binary, so without the assert a crates.io build with `server` would fail blaming trunk. The assert directs the user to a git checkout or SKIP_TRUNK=true.

build.rs unconditionally creates target/assets so rust-embed's #[folder = "target/assets"] resolves at compile time even when no UI was built; the resulting binary compiles and runs but has an empty UI, and the failure is deferred to runtime because serve_index unwraps Assets::get("index.html").

build.rs declares cargo:rerun-if-changed only for frontend/src, frontend/index.html, frontend/styles.css, frontend/Trunk.toml and frontend/Cargo.toml; SKIP_TRUNK has no cargo:rerun-if-env-changed, so changing it on an already-built tree does not re-run the script and the wasm bundle is refreshed only when a listed frontend path changes.

frontend/Trunk.toml pins the build to what src/server.rs expects: dist = "../target/assets" (where the RustEmbed derive reads), target = "index.html" and public_url = "/" so rust-embed's exact-path lookups and server.rs's SPA fallback work at any mount point; the [[proxy]] entries for /graphql, /events, /dats and /romfiles/ apply only to `trunk serve` against a local server on 127.0.0.1:8000 and are ignored by `trunk build`.

A Trunk pre_build hook runs frontend/scripts/fetch-webawesome.sh to vendor Web Awesome and the Font Awesome icons the components need into the gitignored frontend/vendor/, because the UI is served offline by `oxyromon server` and inside the desktop bundle and must never reach a CDN; the script no-ops when its pinned-version-plus-icon-list stamp matches.

Two independent RustEmbed types exist with different gating: src/server.rs embeds target/assets for the SPA, while src/import_dats.rs embeds `data/` for Logiqx header XML used when a DAT names a header file that is absent next to it. The latter is not feature-gated, which is why rust-embed is an unconditional dependency.

CI sets SKIP_TRUNK=true for the whole job and builds the web UI exactly once in a dedicated `cd frontend && trunk build --release` step with trunk pinned to 0.21.14 and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target installed, so every later cargo invocation reuses target/assets instead of recompiling the wasm.

CI runs two clippy passes: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features oxyromon/server` (package-qualified because several workspace packages are selected) and `cargo clippy --no-default-features --features use-rustls,mcp --all-targets`, a dedicated pass that keeps the MCP-stdio-without-web-server combination compiling; the job then builds --release --features server and tests under `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --features oxyromon/server`.

tests/mcp_stdio.rs opens with #![cfg(feature = "mcp")] and drives the real binary (CARGO_BIN_EXE_oxyromon) over piped stdin/stdout with raw JSON-RPC and an isolated OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY, so the stdio transport contract is verified in the lean feature combination rather than through the server build.

dist.sh exports SKIP_TRUNK=true and Cross.toml passes it through into the cross container; for each target it first runs `trunk build --release` on the host (the wasm bundle is target-independent), then `cross build --release --target <t> --features server`, packaging oxyromon alongside the five format-crate CLIs.

The Tauri desktop bundle is built for the host only — Tauri links the platform's own webview, which the cross images lack and for which no cross toolchain exists — and the final step runs with NO_STRIP=true because linuxdeploy's bundled binutils cannot read modern .relr.dyn sections.

The container images do the opposite of CI: neither Dockerfile.archlinux nor Dockerfile.alpine sets SKIP_TRUNK; both install trunk 0.21.14 and the wasm target and run `cargo install --features server`, with Alpine adding gcompat because trunk downloads glibc-linked wasm-bindgen/wasm-opt tools.

The root workspace includes only members = ["crates/*"]; frontend/ and desktop/ are deliberately excluded, each declaring an empty [workspace], its own Cargo.lock and publish = false, so the Leptos/wasm and Tauri/webview dependency trees stay out of the native CLI build. Release profiles diverge accordingly: CLI uses lto = thin / codegen-units = 1 / panic = abort with dev dependencies forced to opt-level 3, while frontend and desktop both use opt-level = "z".

desktop/tauri.conf.json declares externalBin binaries/oxyromon and runs desktop/scripts/stage-sidecar.sh as beforeDevCommand and beforeBuildCommand; the script resolves the target triple from TARGET_TRIPLE or `rustc -vV`, runs `cargo build --release --features server` from the repository root, and copies the binary to desktop/binaries/oxyromon-<triple>[.exe], the triple-suffixed name Tauri requires.

The desktop shell adds no backend: it reserves a free loopback port, spawns the bundled oxyromon as `server --address 127.0.0.1 --port <port>`, polls with TcpStream::connect for up to 30s, opens a WebviewUrl::External window on that origin so the SPA keeps same-origin relative URLs, grants the webview an empty Tauri capability set, and kills the CommandChild on RunEvent::Exit so no orphaned server holds the database.

Publishing is blocked by two mandatory git dependencies recorded with `ponytail` comments: nod pinned to git tag v2.0.0-alpha.12 until it publishes past 2.0.0-alpha.9, and sevenz-rust2 pinned to rev d574d725e717d647c5ae67d3760e8af320920974 of a fork's feat/raw-copy branch until upstream releases push_raw_block; both must return to version requirements before a release.

nod and sevenz-rust2 are unconditional dependencies rather than optional features: 0.25.0 removed the old `nod` and `sevenz` features when RVZ/WBFS and 7z/ZIP support stopped shelling out to dolphin-tool, wit and 7-Zip.

test.sh runs a second coverage pass with --features oxyromon/nod,oxyromon/server,oxyromon/sevenz; the nod and sevenz features no longer exist, so that invocation fails on unknown features while the first (oxyromon/server) pass matches CI.
